original: Plants absorb water through their roots and release some of it as vapor through leaf openings called stomata. This release is transpiration. Clouds contain tiny liquid droplets, ice crystals, or both; they are not simply invisible water vapor.

Rivers carry water downstream, while lakes and wetlands can temporarily store it and influence the timing of its movement. Snow and ice also store water; melting releases liquid water that can enter streams or soil.
